title: Home page thermostat: try each current-temperature look

steps.headline: Press minus and plus a few times and drag the handle. Which look stays clear of everything?
steps.notice: The label follows the line as the room temperature changes; it moves aside for the handle and buttons.
steps.risk: Practice data only; nothing reaches a real thermostat. The room stays at 74° here; use the Climate tab to see the larger dial.

variants.label: Glass pill
variants.summary: A small rounded glass tag with a tiny thermometer and the number, like the page's other chips, hanging off the tip of the line.
variants.risk: It is the busiest of the three: a second little object on a ring that already has a handle. In a very small window it is the biggest label to fit.

variants.label: Just the number
variants.summary: No tag and no word 'Now': only the number, a little bigger and quieter, at the end of the line. The line itself says 'this is now'.
variants.risk: Quietest and cleanest, but nothing says it is the room's temperature. The first time, someone may mistake it for the set point.

variants.label: Flag on the line
variants.summary: The line reaches a little past the ring and ends in a small solid flag reading 'Now 74°', so line and label read as one thing.
variants.risk: Strongest and clearest, and the only one that keeps the word 'Now', but the longer line sticks out past the ring and the flag is the most eye-catching.
